pages.title: Our social purpose | Nord Anglia Education
blocks: It all starts in our local communities, where Nord Anglia schools work closely with local charity and NGO partners to focus on important causes. We want our students to experience first-hand the challenges communities often face tackling issues, and to understand how to influence and drive change as individuals and as part of bigger teams, too.

These experiences help our students develop resilience, teamwork and the creativity to think ‘outside of the box’ — important skills they’ll need in the future workplace. We also encourage our students to deliver meaningful change through local outreach activities, including our Share A Dream programme which teaches social responsibility through fundraising and volunteering about issues that students truly care about.
Every year, NAE students support hundreds of local causes tackling the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals. In the last year alone, Nord Anglia students:
Volunteered over 50,000 hours for local community projects

Nord Anglia Education's inspiring Social Impact Programme with UNICEF challenges our students to think about what they can do to make a difference - locally and globally. Following the UN Sustainable Development 2030 agenda, each year UNICEF and Nord Anglia invite our students to work on a Global Challenge, with themes as wide-ranging as clean energy and peace and justice, to think of innovative solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems. NAE students from Grades 10-12 can even apply to go to the Global Summit in New York, with the chance to speak at the UN’s High Level Political Forum.

Encouraging citizenship starts by making sure our students' voices are heard and given the platforms to deliver positive change. That's why we've created a Student Advisory Board, where elected student leaders from NAE schools across the globe discuss and decide how we'll fund and deliver incredible social impact projects globally in our local communities. Each year they'll award funds to student-led social impact initiatives globally.

Each year, about 2,000 Nord Anglia students travel to our Arusha camp in the foothills of Mount Kilimanjaro, Tanzania. They work with local charities on development projects, including building and extending schools. With each expedition, Nord Anglia students from all around the world help with practical tasks like bricklaying, mixing cement, digging foundations, and plastering — all the time growing in understanding of the lives of local people as well as gaining skills in teamwork and leadership. Above all, students understand their role as considerate global citizens, with an active role in helping others and improving the environment.

Graduated from Champittet in 2000 and is now a journalist

Rouven spent eight years at Champittet (from 1992 to 2000), entering the school as a child and leaving as an adult. The discipline of the boarding house gave him independence and, despite growing up as an only child, helped him learn to live in a community. He has fond memories of his hard-working teachers, who helped develop his critical thinking. Above all, his time at Champittet gave him a strong understanding of the world around us and helped him forge his values.
Graduated from Champittet in 1999, now on the Board of Directors at Swiss Solar City AG

Furcy spent nearly nine years at the Champittet boarding school, following which he earned an MBA, joined a bank, and worked his way up to General Manager. In 2015, he joined three partners in the creation of a start-up that aims to become the largest photovoltaic production plant in Switzerland. Swiss Solar City now supplies nearly 3,000 homes with renewable electricity. For Furcy, Champittet for was a "school of life" where he learned the value of friendship, which has served as his guide ever since.
Graduate from Windermere Prep, now a student-athlete at Columbia University

Yoko, a former Residential Life student at Windermere Preparatory School, balanced her academics with athletics, participating in an off-campus golf league. Yoko is grateful for the enduring friendships she formed and the support of her teachers during her time there. Presently, she continues her educational journey as a student-athlete at Columbia University.
Graduate from the Village School, now attending university in Spain

Leonardo, from Mexico, came to study as a Residential Life student at The Village School. It gave him the chance to connect with students from across the globe, forming a new family that supported him in his quest to improve 1% every single day. Leonardo, who was part of the Entrepreneurship Diploma program during his time at Village, had the opportunity to undertake internships with companies such as Merrill Lynch. Presently, Leonardo is attending IE University in Spain, continuing his educational journey.
Graduate from North Broward and now a music producer and actress

Jacira, a former Residential Life student at North Broward Preparatory School, looks back on her time there with a smile, cherishing the lifelong friendships. Following graduation, she pursued a degree in Business Management in the Arts and Entertainment at Pace University in New York City. Since then, Jacira has embarked on a successful career in the entertainment industry, serving as a music producer and telenovela actress in Lisbon. Recently, she made the move to Los Angeles to further her acting career.
Will my child receive academic monitoring and support after school?

Yes. Our academic coordinators regularly review grades, and your child will receive help during their nightly prep sessions, too. In their core academic courses, your child will be guided by content area specialists, and they can have 1:1 sessions if necessary. Your child’s teachers will also be available both before and after school for extra tuition and direction.
